rationale: Evidence: iteration 6 (outer sensors at x = ±0.06, sensor_size 0.016, kp 7.0, kd 0.2, ki 0.0, last_direction) is the best raced design at 64.74. Iteration 8 changed kd to 0.3 and scored 62.23. Oval progress fell from 0.218 to 0.202 and slalom from 0.103 to 0.096, while oscillation fell only modestly (oval 0.159 to 0.156, s-bend 0.173 to 0.130). Derivative gain 0.3 therefore trades progress for smoothness, and progress drives the score, so kd returns to 0.2. Iteration 7 (kp 6.5) also showed that lowering kp cuts s-bend progress from 0.140 to 0.059, so kp stays at 7.0. Slalom has lost the line once per run in every race (iterations 0 to 8) with progress stuck near 0.10. The one change from iteration 6 is line_loss = search_right, which steers toward the left when the line is lost. It is tested alone against iteration 6 so that the result is not confounded by kd. Change: controller.line_loss set to search_right; kd set to 0.2. Everything else (kp 7.0, ki 0.0, base_speed 1.4, the weights, and all geometry) is unchanged from iteration 6. Expected result: slalom line_loss_events fall toward 0 and slalom progress rises above 0.10, with oval and s-bend progress near iteration 6 (oval about 0.22, s-bend about 0.14). Interpretation: if slalom improves and the oval and s-bend hold, keep search_right. If slalom progress falls or the oval or s-bend worsen, revert to last_direction and address slalom through geometry, such as outer sensors at x = ±0.08. If the robot tracks without off_track but completion_time exceeds 3 s, raise base_speed to 1.6 in a later single-group revision. Measurements wanted: progress, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation per track, plus completion_time and rms_error.
